result.summary: The environment features a marked zebra crosswalk with pedestrian signals and sidewalks on both sides. However, active construction in the foreground creates significant physical and visual obstructions for pedestrians attempting to navigate the crossing.

hazards.name: Open construction trench
hazards.description: An open hole or trench is visible in the immediate foreground left, partially guarded by temporary barricades.

hazards.name: Sidewalk obstruction
hazards.description: Construction barrels and barricades block the natural pedestrian path to the crosswalk.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the crosswalk entrance

hazards.name: Visual obstruction from bus
hazards.description: A large bus stopped near the crossing obscures sight lines between pedestrians and oncoming traffic from the opposite direction.

interventions.title: Improved Work Zone Channelization
interventions.description: Ensure a continuous, clear, and ADA-compliant pedestrian path through the construction area using stable barricades.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulbout)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Program the traffic signal to give pedestrians a 3-7 second head start before the parallel vehicle traffic gets a green light.

result.summary: The image shows a two-lane urban street with a marked zebra crosswalk and sidewalks on both sides. While basic pedestrian infrastructure is present, the crossing is uncontrolled and sight lines are partially obstructed by parked vehicles.

hazards.name: Uncontrolled Crossing
hazards.description: A marked crosswalk exists without any stop signs, traffic signals, or pedestrian warning signs to alert drivers.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Vehicles parked close to the crosswalk on the right side of the image may block sight lines between drivers and pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the roadway beyond the crosswalk

hazards.name: Pavement Degradation
hazards.description: Cracking and debris near the curb ramp on the left side could pose a tripping hazard or impede mobility devices.
hazards.location_in_image: Bottom left corner near the curb

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to improve visibility for both pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Crossing Signage
interventions.description: Install high-visibility pedestrian crossing signs to alert motorists of the crossing location.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct curb extensions to shorten the crossing distance and prevent parking too close to the crosswalk.

result.summary: The image depicts an urban intersection with high-visibility crosswalk markings and sidewalks on both sides. While traffic signals are present, specific pedestrian signal heads are not visible, and some pavement markings show signs of wear.

hazards.name: Worn pavement markings
hazards.description: The continental crosswalk markings and center lane lines show signs of wear and fading.

hazards.name: Lack of visible pedestrian signals
hazards.description: While traffic lights are present, no dedicated pedestrian signal heads are visible to guide crossing timing.

interventions.title: Pavement Marking Refresh
interventions.description: Repaint the continental crosswalk and lane markings to ensure high visibility for drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install dedicated pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to improve safety and predictability for people crossing.

result.summary: The image depicts an urban intersection with sidewalks on both sides and a signalized crossing. While basic infrastructure like pedestrian signals and a marked crosswalk are present, the crosswalk markings are significantly faded and sight lines are partially obstructed by parked vehicles.

hazards.name: Faded Crosswalk Markings
hazards.description: The painted crosswalk is significantly worn, reducing its visibility to approaching motorists.

hazards.name: Sight Line Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles on the left side of the street close to the intersection may block the view between pedestrians and drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the street, upstream of the crosswalk.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk Markings
interventions.description: Replace the faded transverse markings with continental or ladder-style markings to increase visibility.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to improve sight lines for both pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs to shorten the pedestrian crossing distance and further improve visibility by placing pedestrians ahead of parked cars.
